hook: The church musician whose music many call the greatest ever written.

pages.x: Bach was born in Eisenach in 1685 into a huge family of musicians. Orphaned at ten, he went to live with his elder brother, an organist. A story says he secretly copied his brother's locked-away music by moonlight for six months, until his brother found out and took it away.
In 1705 the young organist walked about 400 km to Lübeck to hear the great organist Buxtehude play. He had been given four weeks off. He stayed nearly four months, and his employers were not pleased.

pages.t: Toccata and Fugue in D minor
pages.x: His most famous organ piece opens with a dramatic cry and crashing chords, then races off into a fugue. It has become the sound of haunted castles in films, though some experts now doubt that Bach wrote it.

au.page: Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565

pages.x: When he tried to leave his job at Weimar in 1717, the angry duke had him locked up for a month. Then he was allowed to go, "with disfavour".
In 1721 he sent six concertos to a prince, the Margrave of Brandenburg, perhaps hoping for a job. The margrave probably never had them played. Today they are among the most loved music of the age.
His six suites for solo cello were nearly forgotten for almost 200 years, until a 13-year-old Pablo Casals found an old copy in a second-hand shop in Barcelona in 1890. Every cellist plays them now.
From 1723 until his death he was director of music in Leipzig, writing a new cantata almost every Sunday for years; over 200 survive. He had 20 children, and several became famous composers.

In his last years his eyes failed. Two operations by a travelling eye surgeon made things worse, and he died in 1750. His music fell out of fashion, until in 1829 the young Felix Mendelssohn revived his St Matthew Passion.

Bach is often called the greatest composer of all. His mastery of weaving many melodies together shaped Mozart, Beethoven and every composer since, and his music flies through space on the Voyager probes.
pts: Wrote the Brandenburg Concertos and the cello suites
His music is on the Voyager Golden Record
